newsitem.title: USA: Rockwell to spin off auto component systems.
newsitem.headline: Rockwell to spin off auto component systems.

text.p: Rockwell International Corp Monday said its board approved a plan to spin off its automotive component systems businesses into a new, separately traded, publicly held company.

These businesses had 1996 sales of about $3.1 billion. Following the spinoff Rockwell said it will be an electronics company with global leadership positions in industrial automation, semiconductor systems and avionics and communications.

The spinoff is subject to several conditions, including receipt of a ruling by the U.S. Internal Revenue Service that the transaction would qualify as a tax-free distribution. Rockwell shareowners would receive shares in the new automotive company on a pro rata basis. These shares would be in addition to shares they would continue to hold in Rockwell. Application would be made to list the new shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

Rockwell said it plans to complete the transaction by the end of Rockwell's fiscal year, September 30, 1997. Until the spinoff is completed, the two organizations will operate as a single business. It is expected that the capital structure of the new automotive company would result in a strong credit rating from the first day of operation.

On December 6, 1996, Rockwell completed the divestiture of its aerospace and defense businesses to Boeing Co. By spinning off its automotive activities, the company said it completes its transformation to a global electronics firm.
